Ruth M. Delacroix-Hale MRN: 90417736 10/20/2026 9:20 AM Internist at HSS Paramus
Instructions from Dana Whitlow
Directions for Your Medications Preoperatively
1. Seven (7) days prior to your surgery, do not take the following medications and supplements (these
cause blood thinning):
• Regular Aspirin (325mg) baby aspirin 81mg is permitted if instructed by your doctor.
• Vitamins including Multivitamins
• All Vitamins/Supplements including Glucosamine/ Chondroitin, Fish Oil
• You can continue your vitamin D
2. Four (4) days prior to your joint replacement surgery, do not take the following medications:
• Motrin or Advil (ibuprofen)
• Aleve or Naprosyn (naproxen)
• Any other NSAID
3. Eliquis (apixaban) 2.5 mg: take your LAST dose on the morning of Friday 11/6. Do not take it 11/7,
11/8, 11/9 or the day of surgery. The surgical team will tell you when to restart.
4. Jardiance (empagliflozin): stop three (3) days before sirgery. Last dose on 11/6.
5. Metformin: Do not take 24 hours prior to surgery (no evening dose on 11/9).
6. Tylenol (acetaminophen) is OK to take before surgery if you need something for pain.
8. On the morning of your surgery, take the following medications with a sip of water:
Carbidopa-levodopa (Sinemet)
Metoprolol
